source: NCERT Class X, Science, Ch. 4 (Carbon and its Compounds).

sections.heading: 1. Bonding in Carbon
points: Carbon (atomic number 6) has **4 valence electrons** → forms **four covalent bonds** by **sharing** electrons (tetravalency).
**Covalent bonds** — sharing of electron pairs; covalent compounds have low melting/boiling points, are poor conductors.
**Catenation** — carbon's unique ability to bond with other carbon atoms forming long **chains, branches and rings** → huge number of compounds.
Carbon forms **single, double and triple bonds** (allowing saturated and unsaturated compounds).

sections.heading: 2. Hydrocarbons — Saturated and Unsaturated
points: **Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes)** — only single bonds (e.g. methane CH₄, ethane); burn with a **clean blue flame**.
**Unsaturated hydrocarbons** — **alkenes** (double bond, e.g. ethene C₂H₄) and **alkynes** (triple bond, e.g. ethyne); burn with a **sooty (yellow) flame**; more reactive (undergo addition).
**Isomers** — same molecular formula, different structures (from butane onwards).
**Homologous series** — compounds with same general formula, differing by –CH₂– (14 u); similar chemical properties, gradation in physical properties.

sections.heading: 3. Functional Groups and Key Compounds
points: **Functional group** — an atom/group giving characteristic properties (e.g. –OH alcohol, –COOH carboxylic acid, –CHO aldehyde, >C=O ketone, halo–).
**Ethanol (C₂H₅OH)** — alcohol; reacts with sodium (H₂ released), on dehydration gives ethene; drinking beverages; excess is harmful.

**Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH)** — acetic acid; 5–8% solution = **vinegar**; weak acid; reacts with carbonates (CO₂) and bases; with ethanol gives sweet-smelling **ester (esterification)** → used in perfumes/flavours.

sections.heading: 4. Reactions and Soaps
points: **Combustion** — carbon compounds burn to give CO₂, heat, light (fuels).
**Oxidation** — alcohols oxidised to acids by oxidising agents (alkaline KMnO₄, acidified K₂Cr₂O₇).
**Addition** — unsaturated + H₂ (with Ni catalyst) → saturated (**hydrogenation** of oils → vegetable ghee).
**Substitution** — alkanes react with Cl₂ in sunlight.
**Soaps** = sodium/potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids; clean via **micelles** (hydrophilic head + hydrophobic tail); **detergents** work in hard water (soaps form scum).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Carbon = tetravalent, forms covalent bonds; catenation → chains/rings.
Saturated = single bonds (blue flame); unsaturated = double/triple (sooty flame).
Homologous series differ by –CH₂– (14 u).
Ethanol = –OH; ethanoic acid = –COOH (vinegar = 5–8%); ester = sweet smell.
Hydrogenation (Ni catalyst) converts oils to ghee; soap cleans via micelles.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Carbon is **tetravalent** and forms **covalent** (shared) bonds.
**Unsaturated** hydrocarbons burn with a **sooty/yellow** flame; saturated with a clean **blue** flame.
**Vinegar** = 5–8% ethanoic acid; **esterification** gives sweet-smelling esters.
**Soaps form scum with hard water**; **detergents** do not (work in hard water).
